original_query: SELECT t0.SAL + t1.COMM, SUM(t1.EXPR0) OVER (PARTITION BY t1.JOB RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) FROM (SELECT ENAME, SAL, DEPTNO = 10 AS EXPR0 FROM EMP) AS t0 INNER JOIN (SELECT ENAME, JOB, COMM, SAL + SAL + 100 AS EXPR0 FROM BONUS) AS t1 ON t0.ENAME = t1.ENAME AND t0.EXPR0
rewritten_query:
SELECT e.SAL + b.COMM,
       SUM(b.SAL + b.SAL + 100) OVER (PARTITION BY b.JOB) AS job_sum
FROM EMP e
JOIN BONUS b ON e.ENAME = b.ENAME
WHERE e.DEPTNO = 10;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The boolean expression `DEPTNO = 10 AS EXPR0` used inside ON (`AND t0.EXPR0`) is confusing and non-standard; it is moved to a direct `WHERE e.DEPTNO = 10` predicate, which is equivalent for an inner join and enables clean predicate pushdown.
Both inline subqueries (t0 and t1) are simple projections that can be fully flattened into the main query, removing unnecessary aliasing layers and improving planner readability.
The window frame `RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING` is the default frame when ORDER BY is absent, so it can be omitted without changing semantics.

The join is rewritten as a direct JOIN with the deptno filter applied via WHERE. Recommend indexes: `EMP(DEPTNO, ENAME) INCLUDE (SAL)` to avoid a 45M-row seq scan for the highly selective deptno=10 filter, and `BONUS(ENAME) INCLUDE (JOB, SAL, COMM)` to enable a nested-loop index lookup from the small filtered EMP set instead of building a hash on ~18M BONUS rows.
